description:
We’re a team based on the Gold Coast, Australia, and we love turning complex data into visuals anyone can understand.

Our mission: For Space Apps 2026 we’re tackling Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data. We plan to build an interactive tool that combines NASA Earth data (NASA POWER, SMAP, Landsat) into maps, seasonal risk calendars, and side-by-side crop rotation comparisons, so farmers can see their options at a glance and adapt to a changing climate.
summary:
We developed AcreCast AU, a web app that helps Australian grain farmers decide which crop to plant before they buy seed. A farmer drops a pin or traces their paddock on a map, and the app pulls live NASA POWER data for that spot: daily temperature, rainfall, sunlight and root-zone soil moisture. It replays the coming season against every past season of NASA weather, starting from today's measured soil water, to forecast each crop's yield, harvest date, gross margin per hectare and chance of losing money. It also flags frost, heat and drought risk.

This addresses the challenge by turning NASA Earth observation data into a practical planting decision. Every forecast is checked against official ABARES crop yields; in a 2014-2025 back-test the app picked the best-paying crop in 45 of 72 seasons.

It matters because one wrong crop choice in a dry year can cost a farm hundreds of dollars per hectare. As the climate becomes more variable, farmers need free, location-specific, data-driven advice they can trust, not guesswork.
details:
AcreCast AU: decide which crop to invest in, before you buy seed

What it does
AcreCast AU helps farmers in Australia’s grain belt answer one high-stakes question each season: “Which crop should I plant, and will it make money?” A farmer drops a pin or traces their paddock on a satellite map. AcreCast then forecasts, for six major crops (wheat, barley, canola, chickpeas, grain sorghum and mungbeans):

  • days to harvest and the harvest date
  • expected yield (t/ha)
  • gross margin in AUD for the whole paddock
  • loss risk: how often the crop lost money in past seasons
  • effect on soil nitrogen for the next crop

The results appear as a ranked Season Investment Leaderboard with a clear Top Crop Pick.

How it works

  1. The farmer picks a paddock by map pin, town search, GPS or drawing the fence line, and sets size, sowing date, soil type, irrigation and previous crop.
  2. AcreCast pulls NASA data live. It calls the NASA POWER Daily API (Agroclimatology) for that exact location and downloads 10 years of daily data: maximum and minimum temperature (T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN), rainfall (PRECTOTCORR), root-zone soil moisture (GWETROOT) and solar radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN).
  3. It replays history. Each crop is “sown” in every past year and grown day by day through that year’s real weather, starting from the soil moisture measured today. This gives about ten realistic “next seasons”, including droughts. We deliberately don’t average the weather, because an average year hides crop failures.
  4. It grows the crop. Growing degree days set the harvest date; stored soil water plus rain set the water-limited yield (French–Schultz); sunlight sets the maximum yield; heat or frost at flowering reduces it.
  5. It turns tonnes into dollars using farm-gate prices from ABARES (11 Nov 2026), and ranks crops by average margin per hectare minus a penalty for losing seasons.

We checked the model against real ABARES yields for 2014–2025. It picked the best-paying crop in 45 of 72 seasons, with a typical forecast error of about ±$295/ha. We show that error to farmers instead of hiding it.

Benefits and intended impact

  • Less guesswork, less risk: farmers see the range of outcomes and how often each crop lost money, not just a single number.
  • Climate adaptation: the Climate Stress Time Machine lets farmers test drier (El Niño-style) and hotter seasons before they commit.
  • Healthier soil: nitrogen effects and rotation fit (e.g. pulses adding free nitrogen) encourage rotations that rebuild soil.
  • Free NASA science, made usable: NASA already measures every paddock on Earth; AcreCast turns that data into a decision a farmer can make in minutes, with no technical skills.

How it’s creative

  • Investment framing: crops are ranked like investments, with return on cost, loss risk and a worst-season figure.
  • Simulating every past year (analogue years) instead of averaging, so bad years still show up as risk.
  • Two views of the same data: a plain-language Farmer view, and a NASA Telemetry Mode that shows the raw satellite numbers and formulas for transparency.
  • Paddock-level precision: farmers can trace their own fence line on satellite imagery.

Tools and technologies

  • NASA data: NASA POWER Daily API (Agroclimatology community)
  • Other data: ABARES commodity prices and Australian Crop Report yields; Australian Mungbean Association price
  • Front end: React, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet (interactive maps and paddock drawing)
  • Maps and search: Esri World Imagery, OpenStreetMap, OpenStreetMap Nominatim
  • Hardware: none; it runs in any web browser on a phone or laptop

What our team considered

  • Farmers aren’t data scientists: plain language, traffic-light ratings and dollars instead of indices.
  • Honesty about uncertainty: forecasts are shown as ranges and odds, with the back-test error and a clear “not financial advice” note.
  • Local reality: off-season or out-of-region crops are flagged; soil type, irrigation and the previous crop are inputs; prices and costs are editable.
  • Supporting local expertise, not replacing it: the tool tells farmers to check prices, costs and local agronomy before committing.
  • Limits we’re open about: today’s prices are applied to every past season, costs are indicative, and history gives odds, not a weather forecast.
projectRefs: Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics and Sciences (ABARES)
